newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open weaker, quiet session expected.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open weaker, quiet session expected.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened weaker in quiet trade on Monday after the release of the GDP report for April, with Tuesday's Canada Day holiday expected to keep activity light, dealers said.

"There's not really a lot going on. I think it's going to be kind of quiet today given the holiday tomorrow. We're a little bit weaker again with a strong GDP number in Canada," said one dealer with a bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.20 percent from 3.19 percent at the close of trading on Friday.

Canadian T-bills opened weaker after a report that the country's real gross domestic product, seasonally adjusted, rose 0.8 percent in April after falling 0.2 percent. Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast a rise of 0.6 percent on average for April.
While a stronger Canadian dollar helped to offset the impact of the stronger report, the market "still feels reasonable heavy," the dealer said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.49 percent from 3.48 percent. The one-year T-bill softened to yield 4.0 percent from 3.98 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.45 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
